source: Some interpreter questions every interpreter. Therefore every interpreter is questioned by some interpreter.

claims.interpretation_note: The premise asserts the existence of at least one interpreter who questions all interpreters.

claims.text: Every interpreter is questioned by some interpreter.

evidence.quote: Therefore every interpreter is questioned by some interpreter.

claims.interpretation_note: The conclusion states that for all interpreters, there exists an interpreter who questions them.

translations.formula: (exists x (and (Interpreter x) (forall y (implies (Interpreter y) (Questions x y)))))
translations.reason: The premise asserts existence of an interpreter who questions all interpreters, requiring existential and universal quantifiers.

translations.formula: (forall y (implies (Interpreter y) (exists x (and (Interpreter x) (Questions x y)))))
translations.reason: The conclusion requires universal quantification over interpreters with existential witnesses for each.

interpretation_notes: The premise uses an existential quantifier with universal scope over interpreters, while the conclusion uses universal quantification with existential witnesses. The order of quantifiers distinguishes the two claims.
